messages:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change we see p99.9 latency spikes on INT8 weight-only runs for a subset of traffic. :eyes:

andrew: Which workload/seq-len/payload?

maria: Mostly chat workloads with lots of KV cache hits (short prefixes, many re-uses). Running AWQ 4-bit->INT8 weight-only pipeline on A100 pools. p50 stable but p99.9 jumps ~2.3x.

sasha: Any flamegraphs or traces? Could be slab fragmentation or allocator churn when packing group sizes change.

maria: Uploaded a short perf snippet to the dashboard but here's the local trace snippet:

```
# pprof diff sample (hot slices)
- kv_cache_lookup  45% -> 21%
- pack_serial_write 12% -> 36%
- int8_vector_kernel  30% -> 10%
- scalar_fallback_kernel  3% -> 22%
# net: packing path increased and kernel switched to fallback for some groups
```

kevin: That smells like group-alignment->vector-kernel mismatch. If group size distribution changed we may fall through to the non-vectorized path which has much higher per-token setup.

andrew: Do we have telemetry for "bytes_packed" vs "groups_emitted" per request? Also check slab allocator free lists (hot vs cold).

maria: Currently only counters for kv_cache_hits and pack_ops. I can add bytes_packed and slab_frag_pct, but want to triage quickly.

sasha: Quick hypothesis: new kernel selector prefers the wide vector kernel when group stride >= X, but our packing code started producing more small strides after the packing heuristic tweak (microbatch micro-shifts). That increases pack_serial_write and pushes kernels to scalar fallback.

maria: Agreed. Reproduced on staging by toggling the selector: `KER_SEL=heuristic_v2` vs `KER_SEL=legacy_vector_pref`. With legacy we get earlier vector path and p99 drops back.

andrew: What's the group-size distribution? Try group=32 vs group=64 sweep; AWQ calibration may create different quant blocks depending on group size which interacts with pack alignment.

maria: Quick stats: group-size histogram for affected requests: [16: 48%, 32: 32%, 64: 12%, 128: 8%]. After the packaging tweak we see more 16/32 fragments.

kevin: If AWQ quant blocks are weight-only with group=32, but kernel expects contiguous 64-wide vectors, we will split and run scalar ramps.

maria: Proposed short plan: 1) enable `trace.pack_bytes` and `trace.kernel_chosen` for 10k requests; 2) run group-size sweep on a staging model (16/32/64/128) and collect p99/p999; 3) add temporary fallback policy: if pack_fraction_small > 0.4, force legacy vector chooser.

andrew: Also instrument KV cache eviction stats — micro-batching can bump eviction frequency causing cache misses that change packing characteristics.

sasha: FYI AWQ calibration can change latency slightly if per-group scales are different; check calibration-induced ordering of quant-blocks. We should include a calibration-run flag in the trace.

maria: I'll kick off the traces now. CI-bot, please run the telemetry job `int8-slab-frag-trace` on staging-3.

ci-bot: Job queued: int8-slab-frag-trace. Estimated run: ~12m. Link: https://ci.internal/runs/8923

deploy-bot: Deployed feature/ker-selector-rollback to staging-3 at 2345678915 by maria.

kevin: Once traces land, look for two signals: (1) `pack_serial_write` time per-request vs bytes_packed, (2) kernel fallback ratio. If fallback_ratio correlates with p99 spikes we have a selector bug.

maria: Traces done. Quick findings: fallback_ratio spikes from 2% -> 29% for affected traffic, pack_serial_write avg latency per-op doubled. Attaching snippet: `fallback_ratio=0.29, bytes_packed_median=1.8k, slab_frag=18%`

andrew: Ok that's clear. Short-term: flip selector back for this traffic and add telemetry. Long-term: make selector stride-aware and prefer re-packing into vectors if slab_frag < threshold or attempt group coalescing at pack-time.

sasha: Also add a small allocator change that favors coalescing adjacent small allocations to reduce fragmentation; run microbench with 100k requests.

maria: I'll open a PR with selector rollback + extra metrics + a small coalescer patch for review.

kevin: Nice. Also log AWQ calibration batch id so we can correlate quality vs perf later.

maria: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/2345 — includes tests and telemetry. Can someone review quickly? :pray:

andrew: Reviewing now. If green we'll roll to prod Tuesday with a canary.

sasha: Thanks everyone — good catch. Follow-up: schedule a longer run comparing AWQ vs GPTQ group-size sensitivity (latency + small-slab frac + token quality).

maria: Added to backlog and will coordinate with research for quality traces. Closing loop here. :white_check_mark:
